Please review the following manuscript I wrote.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-osf8lkpx/call-d805e57eb22e47e5949ad0642a892ac7/manuscript.pdf

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, importlib.util, shutil
print(sys.executable)
for mod in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL','pypdfium2']:
    print(mod, importlib.util.find_spec(mod))
for app in ['pdftoppm','pdftotext','pdfinfo','gs']:
    print(app,shutil.which(app))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES', len(r.pages))
print('METADATA', r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    s=p.extract_text()
    texts.append(f'\\n\\n--- PAGE {i+1} ---\\n{s}')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts)[:52000])
PY"

strengths: LPAM addresses a practical stitching problem: residual misalignment along an otherwise usable seam. Repairing selected patches and reconnecting their seams offers a useful modular extension to existing pipelines.

The experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across 79 image pairs, four seam-cutting methods under REW alignment, and five initial alignment methods with baseline seam-cutting. For example, baseline SSIM on SEAGULL improves from 0.638 to 0.697 with LPAM.
Figures 1, 5, and 7 provide qualitative evidence of repaired structural discontinuities. The pipeline diagram and Algorithm 1 make the overall procedure understandable.

The manuscript includes parameter ablations, appropriately credits its principal components and benchmark sources, and provides a code link. The concrete failure discussion in Section 4.5 usefully identifies the tradeoff between local alignment and smooth patch integration.
weaknesses: The main evaluation does not adequately establish overall mosaic quality. Equations (6–9) measure agreement between image patches along the stitching seam, potentially missing deformation and discontinuities at the boundaries of inserted patches. Table 3 exposes this gap: removing the sigmoid improves RMSE, SSIM, and ZNCC on all three datasets, although the sigmoid is justified as preventing other artifacts. Evaluation covering patch boundaries and geometric distortion, or a blinded perceptual comparison, is needed to substantiate the claimed net improvement.

The novelty claims exceed the demonstrated distinction from prior work. Section 2 already describes seam-guided alignment refinement in SEAGULL [22] and dense-matching-based seam/warp estimation in [35], making the subsequent characterization of previous methods as operating on settled pre-aligned images too broad. Postprocessing modularity is useful, but its advantage over these closely related approaches is not established quantitatively; the comparison with Parallax and SEAGULL is limited to a qualitative example in the supplied manuscript.

The seam detector assumes that errors are localized, limiting the claimed independence from initial alignment quality. In Section 3.2, max(Q) <= 1.5 mean(Q) accepts any constant-error seam, even when every pixel has a large error. Such a seam receives no repair. The manuscript does not evaluate this failure condition, sensitivity to k, or performance as initial misalignment becomes more widespread.

The smoothness claim for Equations (4–5) is stronger than the construction supports. At beta = 8, the sigmoid endpoints are approximately 0.018 and 0.982, and the described coordinate-dependent taper does not enforce continuity around the entire rectangular boundary. Fixing boundary labels connects the seams but does not itself ensure continuity of warped image content. Section 4.5 acknowledges related failures, but their frequency and severity remain unmeasured.

Important reproduction details are unclear in the supplied PDF, including the padding used to construct alignment patches, handling of overlapping patches, SIFT-flow settings, input resolutions, and collection and release details for the new 20-pair dataset. The code link is helpful, but these choices affect both quality and runtime.

The efficiency claim needs qualification. Section 4.4 reports LPAM time separately from the host method: on SEAGULL, baseline seam-cutting takes 4.11 seconds and LPAM adds 7.34 seconds, implying approximately 11.45 seconds before initial alignment. This is substantial overhead for the simpler hosts. Total runtime and comparable timings against the seam-guided alternatives would better establish the proposed efficiency advantage.
